simple_definition: A foundry charges a set price for each finished silicon wafer it makes to a customer's design, no matter how many working chips are on it.
technical_definition: Foundry pricing basis in which volume-production revenue is the number of finished wafers shipped times a negotiated per-wafer price for the applicable design/process, adjusted by volume rebates and yield adjustments (GlobalFoundries 20-F).

simple_definition: A credit a foundry gives back to a customer when fewer good chips come off the wafers than agreed.
technical_definition: Variable consideration in foundry contracts, refundable via credit note, that reduces wafer revenue when yields fall below contractual levels; accrued against receivables.

simple_definition: A penalty a customer pays if it buys less than the minimum volume it promised in a long-term supply deal.
technical_definition: Fee under an LTA with minimum volume requirements, estimated as variable consideration and recognised with wafer revenue over the agreement term when not constrained.

simple_definition: The seller books the whole sale at one moment, usually when the goods are shipped or delivered.
technical_definition: Under ASC 606 / IFRS 15, revenue recognised when control of a good transfers at a single point (shipment, delivery, acceptance or licence delivery). Used for wafers (TSMC, GF), chips, tools, spare parts and delivered IP licences.

simple_definition: The seller books revenue gradually while it does the work or while the customer uses the service, instead of all at once.
technical_definition: Revenue recognised as a performance obligation is satisfied over a period - e.g. OSAT services and photomasks (custom output with no alternative use and a right to payment for work done), time-based EDA licences, service contracts and IP subscriptions.
where_used: OSAT, mask maker, EDA, equipment service revenue notes

simple_definition: Money a company expects to earn again and again from the same customers, such as subscriptions, support fees or royalties.
technical_definition: Company-defined (non-GAAP) category. Cadence: revenue recognised over time plus short-term renewable software and committed-spend arrangements (80% in FY2025). PDF Solutions: scheduled items plus historically re-occurring volume items (94% in 2025). Definitions differ across companies.

simple_definition: Revenue a software or IP company books in full at the start of a deal, such as a hardware sale or a perpetual licence.
technical_definition: Cadence's term for revenue recognised at a point in time, mainly hardware, individual IP licences and some software licences with a term over one year.

simple_definition: Signed business a company has not yet delivered and so has not yet counted as revenue.
technical_definition: ASC 606 disclosure of the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied obligations; EDA and IP vendors usually exclude future sales-based royalties (Synopsys US$11.4bn; Arm US$2.07bn).

simple_definition: A deal where a chip designer commits to spend a fixed amount with an EDA vendor and picks the specific tools later.
technical_definition: Non-cancellable commitment of a fixed dollar amount over a period, drawn down against a product list; Synopsys reported US$2.0bn in its backlog at 31 Oct 2025; Cadence describes similar non-cancelable commitments.

simple_definition: A licensee pays a lump sum up front to reduce or replace future per-chip royalties.
technical_definition: Arrangement in IP licensing (Arm) where prepaid or minimum royalty commitments are treated as fixed consideration and recognised as licensing revenue at a point in time.

simple_definition: A licence that lets a chip company design its own processor cores that follow Arm's instruction set, rather than use Arm-designed cores.
technical_definition: Arm licence to architecture IP including future version extensions over contracts of 3 to 20 years; consideration is allocated between available architecture and deferred future extensions.

simple_definition: A fee a fab-software vendor earns that goes up or down with how many wafers its customer produces.
technical_definition: PDF Solutions' volume-based revenue tied to customers' wafer manufacturing volumes, recognised in the usage period and accrued from estimates before customer reports.

simple_definition: A chipmaker pays a tool maker to hold a place in its production schedule for a machine it will receive later.
technical_definition: ASML contract term giving ASML a right to payment for systems through reservation of a production slot and/or on delivery, with the balance on final acceptance; most contracts also require a down payment.

simple_definition: A multi-year framework deal in which a chipmaker agrees to buy a number of tools at negotiated discounts.
technical_definition: ASML framework agreement covering up to five years with multiple performance obligations (systems, options, installation, warranties), discounts, free goods/credits; individual sales orders draw down on it. KLA also uses volume purchase agreements with credits and incentives.

simple_definition: When a chip company's own factory unit 'sells' wafers to its own product units at prices meant to look like market prices.
technical_definition: Intel Foundry records intersegment wafer and back-end service revenue from Intel Products at prices intended to approximate market pricing; external customers were US$307m of its 2025 revenue.

simple_definition: A right that lets a distributor send back slow-selling chips to the maker in exchange for others.
technical_definition: Distributor right to return a portion of inventory for other products; treated by chipmakers (Microchip) as variable consideration estimated with the expected-value method.

simple_definition: Whether a distributor books the full selling price as its revenue (it owns the goods) or only its fee (it just arranges the sale).
technical_definition: ASC 606 test: principal if it controls the goods (inventory risk, pricing discretion, fulfilment), recording gross revenue; agent if it arranges supply by another party, recording the net fee (Avnet, Arrow).

simple_definition: Money a chip company pays partners to promote its products, which it counts as a reduction of its sales.
technical_definition: Partner payments earmarked for market-segment development; NVIDIA accounts for MDFs and reseller rebates as reductions to revenue.

simple_definition: A gas company builds a plant at or next to a big customer's site and pipes gas to it under a very long contract.
technical_definition: Linde distribution mode: total-requirement contracts typically 10-20 years with minimum purchase requirements and price escalation, consideration indexed to price indices, recognised over time as delivered.

simple_definition: Money a customer pays a chipmaker up front to guarantee supply, returned if it buys the promised amount.
technical_definition: Microchip LTSA (3-5 years): upfront deposit plus minimum purchase commitments in exchange for assured supply; deposit returned if commitments met, otherwise retained and recognised as revenue.
